correctness.rationale: Cyclic expansion gives D4=4Tr(A^3B+AB^3+A^2B^2-3ABAB). The two Hilbert–Schmidt squares are respectively Tr(A^3B+AB^3-2A^2B^2) and 2Tr(A^2B^2-ABAB). Their weighted sum is exactly D4, for positive finite matrices and, by Schatten Holder, all positive Schatten-four pairs. Noncommuting two-dimensional P,Q have D4=3, commutator energy 1/2 and first square zero, giving the optimal coefficient six; commuting joint eigenpairs characterize D4=0. The standalone exact-rational checker passed 564 pairs; the analytical trace identity proves the universal quantifier.

value.rationale: The exact noncommutative two-square decomposition upgrades a classic trace inequality to a sharp dimension-free stability certificate. It bounds the commutator energy by one sixth of the defect, and the optimal coefficient is attained in a noncommuting rank-one family; the zero-defect equality classification is complete for all positive Schatten-four operators. This identifies a structural obstruction with potential use when near equality is used to diagnose near commutation, beyond a named numerical example.
